findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.explanation: Without a CSP, browsers cannot restrict which scripts, styles, or resources the page may load, making XSS attacks more impactful.
findings.fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header. Start with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' and progressively tighten it.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors missing
findings.explanation: Without framing protection, this page can be embedded in an attacker-controlled iframe, enabling clickjacking attacks.
findings.fix: Add X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN), or add frame-ancestors 'self' to your Content-Security-Policy.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff missing
findings.explanation: Without nosniff, some browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute content as a different type than declared (e.g., execute a JSONP endpoint as a script).

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.explanation: Without Referrer-Policy, the browser's default behaviour may leak full URLs (including query parameters with sensitive data) to third-party sites via the Referer header.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.explanation: Without Permissions-Policy (formerly Feature-Policy), powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation) may be accessible to embedded third-party iframes.
findings.fix: Add a Permissions-Policy header to restrict which browser features this page and its embedded content may use.

findings.title: Cookie 'session_id' missing HttpOnly flag
findings.explanation: The cookie 'session_id' is accessible to JavaScript. If the site has an XSS vulnerability, an attacker can steal this cookie.
findings.fix: Add the HttpOnly flag: Set-Cookie: name=value; HttpOnly; ...

findings.title: Site is served over plain HTTP
findings.explanation: The site is not using HTTPS. All traffic including credentials and session tokens is transmitted in plaintext and can be intercepted by anyone on the network path.
findings.fix: Obtain a TLS certificate and configure the server to serve all content over HTTPS. Redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS.

findings.title: .git/HEAD exposed
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, size=21 bytes, body starts with 'ref: refs/heads/main\n'
findings.explanation: Git repository HEAD file is publicly accessible
findings.fix: Remove or restrict access to /.git/HEAD. Ensure your web server does not serve sensitive files. Add these paths to your .gitignore and review deployment scripts.

findings.title: .env file exposed
findings.fix: Remove or restrict access to /.env. Ensure your web server does not serve sensitive files. Add these paths to your .gitignore and review deployment scripts.

findings.title: .DS_Store file exposed
findings.fix: Remove or restrict access to /.DS_Store. Ensure your web server does not serve sensitive files. Add these paths to your .gitignore and review deployment scripts.

findings.title: backup.zip exposed
findings.fix: Remove or restrict access to /backup.zip. Ensure your web server does not serve sensitive files. Add these paths to your .gitignore and review deployment scripts.

findings.title: robots.txt hints
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, size=32 bytes, body starts with 'User-agent: *\nDisallow: /admin/\n'
findings.explanation: robots.txt is present; review Disallow rules for sensitive paths
findings.fix: Remove or restrict access to /robots.txt. Ensure your web server does not serve sensitive files. Add these paths to your .gitignore and review deployment scripts.

findings.title: Server header reveals version
findings.explanation: The 'server' header reveals the software product and version (Apache/2.4.49). This helps attackers identify unpatched software and target known CVEs.
findings.fix: Remove or redact the 'server' header. In Apache: ServerTokens Prod. In nginx: server_tokens off. In PHP: expose_php = Off.

findings.title: X-Powered-By header reveals version
findings.explanation: The 'x-powered-by' header reveals the software product and version (PHP/7.4.3). This helps attackers identify unpatched software and target known CVEs.
findings.fix: Remove or redact the 'x-powered-by' header. In Apache: ServerTokens Prod. In nginx: server_tokens off. In PHP: expose_php = Off.

findings.title: Directory listing is enabled
findings.evidence: Page body matches directory listing pattern: '<title>\\s*Index of\\s*/'
findings.explanation: The web server is configured to display a list of files in a directory when no index file is present. This can expose sensitive files, source code, backups, and internal structure to attackers.
findings.fix: Disable directory listing in your web server configuration. Apache: Options -Indexes. nginx: autoindex off. IIS: Disable Directory Browsing in site settings.

findings_summary: LOW: X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors missing
MEDIUM: Site is served over plain HTTP
